newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to send 700 peacekeepers to Albania.
newsitem.headline: Greece to send 700 peacekeepers to Albania.

text.p: Greece said on Monday it would send about 700 men to Albania as part of an Italian-led multinational security force to protect humanitarian relief operations in the lawless neighbouring country.
"Greece will participate in the multinational force with about 700 soldiers. We have asked for them to be stationed around Tirana," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas said.
Albania's parliament, dominated by President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party, voted on Sunday 97 to 1 to pass the law allowing the U.N.-approved multinational force.

The 5,000-strong force is being put together after receiving approval from the United Nations on Friday. Among the countries expected to contribute troops are Italy, France, Greece, Spain, Portugal, Romania and Turkey.
About half of the force will be deployed initially and the rest will be in reserve. The first men were expected to arrive in Albania in the next few weeks.
Reppas said final details of the deployment would be decided during a meeting of military commanders in Rome on Wednesday.
Italy and Greece, Albania's EU neighbours, have expressed deep concern that the crisis sweeping the Balkan country could trigger a massive wave of illegal immigration.
Both countries were flooded by illegal Albanian workers in 1991 and 1992 after a communist regime collapsed after 45 years in power. Some 350,000 Albanians leave and work illegally in Greece.
Reppas said Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino would visit Greece on Wednesday for talks with Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
